heroHeadline: NHS Hits 18-Week Target, CPI Falls to 2.8% — Labour Crisis Stabilises as Starmer Presses EU Alignment Agenda
heroSubtitle: NHS England met its 18-week waiting time target for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, with the list falling to 7.11 million — the largest monthly drop in 17 years. ONS data released 21 May showed UK CPI inflation at 2.8% in April (down from 3.3% in March), with services inflation at a four-year low of 3.2%, raising market expectations of a Bank of England rate cut in June. Prime Minister Keir Starmer survived the immediate post-Streeting crisis: LabourList tracking shows 159 Labour MPs backing him vs 97 demanding resignation — below the 81-MP threshold to trigger a formal leadership contest. Starmer pressed ahead with his EU alignment agenda, pledging to bring Britain 'closer to the heart of Europe'. The SNP's newly elected minority Scottish Parliament began coalition negotiations, with First Minister Swinney targeting an independence referendum by 2028.
footerNote: Data sourced from UK Parliament Hansard, The National Archives, ONS, Bank of England, Electoral Commission, NHS England, BBC, Reuters, FT, The Guardian, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, CNN, CNBC, ITV News, and major academic institutions including LSE, Chatham House, and the Resolution Foundation.
